item.description:
**Company Description**
At SAP, you will be part of a global environment that values shared learning, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You will work across international teams, exchange knowledge openly, and develop alongside colleagues committed to advancing machine learning engineering practices. SAP's culture encourages curiosity, inclusion, and growth, giving you opportunities to contribute meaningfully no matter your level.
**Job Description**
**What you'll bring** You have hands-on experience building and operating ML systems in production, with solid skills in Python, data pipelines, and ranking or retrieval systems.
* Python proficiency and hands-on experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or scikit-learn. * Experience building or maintaining data pipelines at scale. Spark, Databricks, Delta Lake, or equivalent. * Solid knowledge of ranking, retrieval, or recommendation systems; experience with multi-signal fusion or semantic search is a plus. * SQL fluency and comfort working with large-scale columnar data stores. * End-to-end ML ownership across training, evaluation, serving, and monitoring; experience with A/B experimentation is a plus. * Degree not required for this role.
We also look for people who build trust naturally, communicate with clarity, keep the customer at the centre of what they do, and bring emotional intelligence and genuine problem-solving ability to the challenges they face.
In addition to the skills and experience specific to this role, all positions at SAP require candidates to be comfortable using AI tools, including agentic AI. Candidates should be able to create effective inputs. They must automate routine tasks and evaluate the quality of AI-generated outputs. Additionally, they should promote the adoption of AI practices within their teams.
**What you'll build** You will build and maintain ML systems that power personalized learning experiences for enterprise employees, covering offline pipelines, online ranking, and feedback loops.
* Build and maintain offline ML pipelines for signal extraction, feature engineering, and candidate generation. * Contribute to request-time ranking logic that fuses signals from multiple ML routes into a personalized result. * Extract and transform employee signals; skills, proficiency, and learning history, into reusable, scenario-agnostic feature snapshots. * Design and maintain quality gates that validate ML pipeline outputs before they reach the serving layer. * Build the experimentation infrastructure. This includes A/B schemas, offline evaluation, and ablation testing. These tools will help measure improvements accurately and thoroughly. * Collaborate with Data Scientists, Architects, and Product to refine algorithms and ship end-to-end ML systems.
**Where you belong** You will join a small, high-ownership pod building personalized learning experiences for enterprise employees at scale. The team runs offline ML pipelines, online ranking, and feedback loops in production, processing signals from millions of employees. You will work directly alongside Data Scientists, Architects, and Product from day one, shipping end-to-end ML systems.
**Additional Information**
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

We ultimately believe in unleashing all talent and creating a better world. item.description:
**XPENG** is a leading smart technology company at the forefront of innovation, integrating advanced AI and autonomous driving technologies into its vehicles, including electric vehicles (EVs), electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and robotics. With a strong focus on intelligent mobility, XPENG is dedicated to reshaping the future of transportation through cutting-edge R&D in AI, machine learning, and smart connectivity.
**The Mission:** We are building the next generation of L4 autonomous vehicles. Moving beyond traditional modular stacks, we are developing large-scale **Vision-Language-Action (VLA)** models and **World Models** to handle the infinite long-tail scenarios of global driving. As a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will architect the transition from behavior cloning to intelligent, zero-shot decision-making in diverse global markets.
**Key Responsibilities**
* Architectural Leadership: Lead the design of end-to-end VLA architectures, bridging multi-modal perception with high-level linguistic reasoning and precise action generation. * World Model Development: Drive R&D in generative world models (latent dynamics) to create high-fidelity, controllable driving simulations for closed-loop training and evaluation. * Policy Evolution: Apply Advanced RL (Online/Offline) and IL to refine driving policies, focusing on long-horizon planning and complex multi-agent interactions. * Scaling & Data Strategy: Define scaling laws for driving foundation models, overseeing data curation, automated labeling, and post-training at a multi-billion parameter scale. * Global Generalization: Lead the model’s adaptation strategy for overseas road conditions, ensuring robust performance across varying traffic laws and driving cultures.
**Qualifications**
* 5-8 years of expertise in Deep Learning, with a significant track record in VLM, VLA, or Embodied AI. * Proven experience in training and deploying Foundation Models (Transformers, LLMs) at scale. * Deep understanding of Sequential Decision Making, World Models, or Policy Gradient methods. * Mastery of PyTorch and expertise in distributed training (DeepSpeed, Megatron, etc.). * A "Product-First" mindset: The ability to balance cutting-edge research with the deterministic requirements of L4 production vehicles.
**What Do We Provide**
* A fun, supportive and engaging environment * Infrastructures and computational resources to support your ML model development/research. * Opportunity to work on cutting edge technologies with the top talent in the field. * Opportunity to make significant impact on transportation revolution by the means of advancing autonomous driving * Competitive compensation package * Snacks, lunches, dinners, and fun activities

item.title: Senior ML Applied Scientist , Frontier AI Startup Team - Amazon Web Services (AWS)
item.description:
**Description** AI-native startups now train their own models, post-train open-weight models for their products, and serve inference at volumes where cost per output decides their margins. The startup team of the AWS Frontier AI Services puts applied scientists to work directly with those founders and their engineers. We're hiring a Senior Applied Scientist in North America to own those engagements with our strategists end to end: scope the problem with the founding team, design and run the experiments, and ship working code into the startup's stack on AWS. The problems are open-ended and the timelines run in weeks, so your scientific judgment sets both the approach and the bar for done.
Key job responsibilities
* Work directly with founders, CTOs and ML leads at AI startups to define the problem and agree on a production target and an evaluation plan. Then deliver against them in six-to-twelve-week engagements, with the startup's own engineers working alongside you. * Improve model quality for the startup's use case by post-training open-weight models. That covers supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning (for example GRPO), distillation, and the synthetic data and evaluation sets that show whether it worked. * Cut training and inference cost and latency on NVIDIA GPUs and AWS Trainium. Profile where the compute goes, apply quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, batching, parallelism and kernel-level tuning, and measure cost per output before and after. * Invent new methods when published ones fall short of the customer's target, and publish the results at peer-reviewed venues, on AWS blogs and as open-source code. * Turn each engagement into assets the next one can reuse: reference implementations, evaluation harnesses and playbooks. Take the gaps you find in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker and AWS Trainium back to those service teams as specific requests. * Raise the science bar on the team. Review experiment designs and code, mentor scientists and engineers, and help account teams and strategists judge which startup requests need a scientist.
A day in the life
You start the day on a call with the CTO of a robotics startup whose vision-language model misses objects in low light. Before anyone changes the model, you agree on an evaluation set built from their own camera footage. Mid-morning you check an overnight reinforcement-learning run for another startup: reward is up but two task categories regressed, so you write up why and what to try next. After lunch you join an AWS account manager and a GenAI strategist to scope a request from a voice AI company that needs lower inference latency before it scales up. You leave with a two-week profiling plan and one go/no-go metric. You end the day reviewing a teammate's experiment design and editing a workshop paper drawn from last quarter's engagement.
**About The Team** We're applied scientists and GenAI strategists working as one team with venture-backed, AI-native startups, from the first discovery call to a model running in production. The work spans large language and vision-language models, agents, voice, multimodal retrieval and physical AI, including world and action models. We judge an engagement by what the startup ships. Startups make platform decisions in weeks, so we scope quickly, share results early, and say plainly when something isn't working. This role focuses on startups in North America. You'll work with AWS account teams, solutions architects and service teams, and with Amazon's wider science community.
**Basic Qualifications**
* PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience * Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
**Preferred Qualifications**
* Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc. * Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc. * 6+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience

item.title: Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Perception, Simulation Realism - Waymo
item.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
About the Team: The "Oracle" for Autonomous Driving
Our mission is to build the high-fidelity, platform-agnostic Ground Truth (GT) engine that powers the next generation of autonomous vehicle (AV) simulation and evaluation. We function as the "Oracle"—by reprocessing onboard logs offline using state-of-the-art ML Foundation Models, we generate semantic signals that significantly outperform real-time onboard software.
Since our inception in early 2025, we have moved from concept to a fully operational end-to-end ML solution. As we head into 2027, we are scaling this "Oracle" to become the backbone of all large-scale evaluation, enabling the business to test software at a level of rigor and realism previously thought impossible.
The Role
We are looking for a strategic technical leader to drive the ML perception architecture for Sim GroundTruth. This role sits at the critical intersection of cutting-edge perception ML research, foundation models, and massive-scale offline data engineering. As a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will serve as the chief technical authority for our perception models, guiding and mentoring ML engineers to solve the "technical moat" of high-fidelity 3D perception and ML inference at a petabyte scale.
Key Responsibilities
* Scalable ML Architecture & Signal Expansion: Architect a modular, extensible ML framework capable of rapidly absorbing a growing list of complex signal requirements. You will lead the transition from specialized models to unified Foundation Model architectures that maintain "Oracle" quality while scaling to hundreds of new semantic categories. * Strategic Ownership & Quality Leadership: Define the multi-year roadmap for signal quality, coverage, and reliability. Your mandate is to ensure our signals don’t just match onboard software—they set the industry benchmark for ground truth accuracy. * ML Scale & Inference Efficiency: Lead the optimization of high-fidelity perception model inference and compute efficiency across massive, petabyte-scale datasets, collaborating with backend infrastructure leads to support rigorous, high-frequency evaluation. * Stakeholder & Ecosystem Growth: Act as the primary interface for "Application Owners" across the company. You will translate complex simulation needs into technical requirements and aggressively grow our customer base to ensure every major software launch is "Oracle-validated." * Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Serve as the senior technical leader and mentor for ML perception engineers, championing modeling best practices, architectural rigor, and driving technical execution on mission-critical P0 perception initiatives.
**Requirements**
* Education: Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related field (PhD preferred). * Technical Leadership: Proven track record of senior technical leadership setting technical vision, architecting complex ML systems, and mentoring senior engineers and research scientists. * Cross-Stakeholder Alignment: Proven track record of navigating complex organizations to gather requirements from diverse customers and aligning them into a unified technical roadmap. You can negotiate Roles & Responsibilities (R&R) across competing priorities. * Technical Depth: Hands-on experience with an ability to technically lead ICs daily, including deep knowledge of codebases, eval/data pipelines, and model architectures. * ML & Perception Expertise: Deep understanding of Foundation Models (VLMs or MMLMs) and computer vision / perception architectures (e.g., Transformers, 3D detection, scene reconstruction), specifically in the context of post-training, fine-tuning, or inference-time scaling. * Proficiency: Expert-level skills in Python, Numpy, and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch or JAX).
**Preferred Qualifications**
* Systems Engineering: Experience building and scaling distributed systems or data pipelines at a petabyte scale. * Object Detection & AV Perception: Deep expertise in 2D and 3D object detection, multi-modal sensor fusion (camera, LiDAR), tracking, and offboard ground-truth generation for autonomous vehicles. * Software Rigor: Proficiency in C++ and experience with production-grade ML deployment. * Academic Impact: A strong publication record at top-tier conferences (CVPR, ICRA, NeurIPS) or leadership in major open-source projects.
The expected base salary range for this full-time position across US locations is listed below. Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process.
Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements.
Salary Range
$298,000—$368,000 USD

item.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation - Thomas To
item.description:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.
We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups:
* Internal partners, including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators. * Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages. * The research community, through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues.
The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward.
**What You'll Be Doing**
* Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API. * Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row. * Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results. * Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap. * Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists. * Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences.
**What We Need To See**
* BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). * 6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries. * Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on. * Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost. * Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools. * Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit.
**Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd**
* Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library. * RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL. * Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses. * Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding. * Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization.
NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, and you want to build the open-source infrastructure behind trustworthy user simulation, we want to hear from you!

item.title: Principal Machine Learning Engineer - Matchmaking - Roblox
item.description:
Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.
At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
Matchmaking is a critical stage downstream of Discovery and Search. Once a player chooses a game to play, matchmaking assigns them to a server for that game. That decision shapes who they play with, the network latency they experience, and the quality of their session. item.description:
**Description** AWS Elemental builds media services used by broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video. Elemental Inference is the applied machine learning team within that organization. We develop models that understand and transform live and file-based video, producing capabilities such as intelligent reframing, highlight detection, video enhancement, and contextual metadata for advertising and content discovery. Our work reaches customers through the same media workflows that carry major live events, always-on channels, and large on-demand libraries.
As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will develop new machine learning approaches and carry the strongest ideas into production. Current work spans multimodal video, audio, and language models; spatial and temporal understanding; active-speaker and point-of-interest detection; scene retrieval; video super-resolution; and learned methods for improving compression. These problems rarely have a single accepted metric or a ready-made dataset. You will help define the task itself, determine what evidence is needed, and build evaluation methods that reflect the experience of people watching and working with the resulting video.
This role combines applied research with the practical demands of a real-time media service. You will design datasets and objectives, train models at scale, run controlled comparisons, and investigate failures. You will also work closely with engineers to export, optimize, and deploy those models. A result is not finished when it performs well in a notebook. It must preserve its quality after conversion, fit within GPU memory, meet latency and throughput targets, handle the temporal behavior of live video, and operate at a cost customers can sustain.
You will be a technical leader on the team as well as an individual contributor. The role calls for someone who can take an ambiguous customer problem, separate the scientific questions from the engineering constraints, and lead a team toward a defensible answer. You will review experiments and models, mentor other scientists and engineers, and improve the shared methods the team uses for training and evaluation. Strong judgment matters here. So does the ability to explain a complicated result clearly, including its limitations, to people from several disciplines.
We welcome candidates with deep experience in computer vision, multimodal learning, video processing, or related areas. Direct media experience is valuable but not required. A scientist who has solved difficult problems in another field, understands how to test ideas rigorously, and wants to learn the video domain can also succeed in this role.
Key job responsibilities
Lead the formulation of ambiguous video problems into research plans with clear datasets, objectives, baselines, evaluation protocols, and production acceptance criteria.
Develop models for multimodal video understanding and generation, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.
Develop models for multimodal video understanding and description, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.
Build evaluations that measure the behavior customers will see. Depending on the problem, this may include task accuracy, factual support, temporal localization, retrieval quality, perceptual video quality, rate-distortion performance, or human review.
Take models from research code to production-ready artifacts. Partner with engineers on model export, reduced-precision inference, quantization, numerical parity, accelerator-specific optimization, and integration with serving systems and video pipelines.
Balance model quality against latency, throughput, GPU memory, context limits, and operating cost. Diagnose problems across training stability, data quality, precision, compilation, serving, and live temporal behavior.
Build reusable mechanisms for dataset management, experimentation, model comparison, regression detection, and performance measurement rather than solving each research problem in isolation.
Review scientific work and production code. Identify weak comparisons, data leakage, unsupported conclusions, untested edge cases, and operational risks before they reach customers.
Work with product managers, software engineers, and other scientists to make scope and design decisions. Use evidence to resolve disagreement and communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what further work is worth doing.
Mentor scientists and engineers in experimental design, machine learning methods, video evaluation, and production ML practices.
Contribute applied research through internal technical reports, patents, and publications at appropriate conferences or workshops.
**About The Team** AWS Elemental provides a portfolio of cloud media services built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. Our technology supports some of the world's largest live broadcasts as well as 24/7 channels and on-demand content. The broader organization brings together expertise in video coding, image processing, distributed systems, advertising, and the operational demands of professional media.
Elemental Inference applies machine learning across that video pipeline. The team works on video understanding and enhancement, contextual metadata, smart composition, event detection, retrieval, and compression. Some projects use large multimodal models that combine video, audio, and language. Others use specialized temporal or spatial models designed for a narrow task and a strict real-time budget. We choose the approach that fits the customer problem rather than forcing every problem into the same model family.
Scientists on the team own more than model architecture. They build and govern datasets, develop annotation methods, train on distributed GPU infrastructure, and create evaluations that can reveal where a model succeeds or fails. They compare internal models with external alternatives and track accuracy, perceptual quality, latency, memory use, and cost. When a model is ready to ship, scientists work with engineers to convert it into a verified production artifact and integrate it into the inference service or the underlying video-processing engine.

**Preferred Qualifications**
* Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc. * Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.
If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.
**AI Researcher (World Models & VLA)** ****What You’ll Do**** A visionary Machine Learning Engineer to join our founding team who will help bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. We are actively hiring across three core specialized subcategories: AI Research, Post-Training Optimization, and Data Engineering.
* Research and develop cutting edge RL and distillation techniques for trajectory planning * Integrate emerging research from the broader AI community, identifying and prototyping the most promising solutions * Design and deploy end-to-end multimodal models that translate real-time visual perception and high-level behavioral goals into physical vehicle actuation * Develop interactive world models from raw multi-sensor logs, allowing the team to re-simulate events and query what a vehicle would see if it altered its trajectory * Ensure core autonomous driving models can seamlessly adapt to novel urban environments and edge cases * Partner with validation and QA teams to run model releases through rigorous simulated scenarios, detecting regressions and identifying systemic performance bottlenecks.
****What We’re Looking For****
* 10+ years of non-internship professional MLE experience. * Deep expertise in applying AI Transformers to robotics, physical actuation, or spatial-temporal data. * Proven track record designing or training multimodal systems, large-scale VLA models, or generative Diffusion models. * Strong background in Sensor Fusion, combining inputs from Cameras, LiDAR, and Radar. * Fluency in PyTorch or JAX for training large-scale models. * Experience with multi-task learning, Birds-Eye-View (BEV) frameworks, representation learning, or data tokenization is highly preferred. * Proficiency in Python and familiarity with C++.
**Post-Training & Optimization** ****What You’ll Do****
* Own the post-training lifecycle by distilling, quantizing, and optimizing massive models to run with low latency on vehicle edge hardware. * Profile real-time inference pipelines to identify and eliminate CPU, GPU, and memory bandwidth bottlenecks on the vehicle. * Work with low-level hardware, electrical, and firmware teams to iterate on custom carrier boards, sensor interfaces, and GPUs on edge devices. * Benchmark and deploy models utilizing hardware-accelerated runtimes (e.g., TensorRT, CUDA) to minimize inference times under strict constraints.
****What We’re Looking For****
* 10+ years of non-internship professional MLE experience. * Strong background in machine learning engineering with a focus on model optimization, distillation, and deployment. * Hands-on experience optimizing models for edge deployment or custom embedded GPU targets. * Deep understanding of profiling tools and debugging resource constraints across CPU/GPU boundaries. * Experience with modern deep learning frameworks (PyTorch or JAX) and runtime compilation. * Robust programming skills in Python and C++. * Familiarity with low-level camera/sensor interfaces and robotics hardware is a significant plus.
**Data & Long-Tail Scenarios** ****What You’ll Do****
* Architect automated pipelines to ingest, filter, and identify rare, high-value, and long-tail scenarios out of multi-petabyte multi-sensor datasets. * Target and extract complex structural corner cases from real-world driving logs to continuously feed, challenge, and improve our end-to-end behavior models. * Iterate closely with QA, testing, and simulation teams to transform ambiguous real-world anomalies into concrete data blocks for simulation testing. * Implement programmatic data curation, active learning strategies, and statistical quality metrics to optimize the signal-to-noise ratio of our training pipelines.
****What We’re Looking For****
* 10+ years of non-internship professional MLE experience. * Professional experience building data curation pipelines, active learning workflows, or data mining architectures for massive physical datasets. * Strong familiarity with robotics data structures and spatial frameworks, including Birds-Eye-View (BEV) or spatial tokenization. * Experience processing and structuring raw data from Cameras, LiDAR, and Radar. * Expert-level proficiency in Python, data engineering frameworks, and PyTorch/JAX. * Exceptional ability to navigate, structure, and derive signal from highly ambiguous, messy, or undefined real-world data distributions.
